seen_animation: A side-view bus drawn in black lines (stepped roof at the front on the left, four window panes hanging from the roof line, a front and rear vertical edge, a floor line, two small wheels) sits on a grey street with grey house outlines behind it. In frames 1-8 it sits slightly right of centre and grows slightly. From frames 9-12 it grows larger and its front edge moves left while the rear edge reaches the right frame edge and the rear wheel is cut by the frame. In frames 13-16 the bus fills the frame: only the front edge, the stepped roof, three window panes and the front wheel remain visible, with the rear off the right edge. The scenery changes from houses to a lower band of building outlines as the bus grows.
seen_film: A 1940s city bus ('Mission') drives along a sloped street toward the camera and slightly left, front on the left side of the bus. In frames 1-8 it is mid-frame in front of a grocery and a corner building, growing slowly; the camera pans to follow. In frames 9-12 it is larger, front moving left, rear reaching the right frame edge. In frames 13-16 the bus fills the frame, front at the left edge, rear and rear wheel out of frame on the right, front wheel large in lower centre.
named_subject: a city bus seen from the side
evidence: Judged from still frames only. Front edge positions track the film: e.png frame 1 front at about 40% of frame width (film 1 the same), frame 9 about 30% (film 9 about 30%), frame 17 about 18% (film 17 about 18%), frame 25 about 7% (film 25 about 6%). The rear wheel reaches the right edge at e.png 17-20 and is gone from 21, as in f.png 17-21. Growth across e.png 1-25 is gradual with no frame-to-frame size jumps; g.png shows the front edges stepping evenly left and the drawing centres advancing in order with no reversals. The body keeps the doodle's construction in every frame: stepped front roof, four panes hanging from the roof line, open-ended lines, single-stroke edges.
primary_gap: The wheels are small hexagonal rings cut through their centres by the floor line, whereas the doodle's wheels are wide flattened ovals hanging below the floor line, so the lower half of the bus reads less like c.png than the upper half.
closes_when: In every frame the floor line runs above the wheels and each wheel is drawn as a wider flattened oval (about a fifth of the body length) hanging below it, as in c.png.
protect: Keep the timing and placement that match the film (front edge positions and growth per frame, rear wheel exiting at frames 17-21), the steady frame-to-frame growth with no pops, the stepped roof and the four hanging window panes in the doodle's stroke style, and the sparse grey scenery that does not compete with the bus.
identity_gap: The body matches c.png, but the wheels are smaller, more angular and sit on the floor line instead of being flattened ovals below it.
